transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess it’s a little embarrassing to say, but… I’ve been having trouble at night with food. It’s not every second or anything, but once I start picking at leftovers, I kind of lose the thread. Part of me is thinking, “That’s enough, Alejandro,” but my hand just keeps going back for more anyway. I thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets worse, if that makes sense.
When you're picking at those leftovers, do you feel like you're in control of how much you're eating?

Not really, no. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but once I start, it’s like the reasonable part of me is saying, “Okay, that’s enough, Alejandro,” and then my hand still keeps going back for more. So… I guess in that moment I don’t feel very in control.
Does this loss of control when eating usually happen at night?

Yes… mostly at night. It’s usually when I’m picking at leftovers late, after everything’s quiet. I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Alejandro,” but then I keep reaching back for more anyway. It’s not something I’m proud of, but that’s kind of what’s been happening.
Do you usually feel guilty after these late-night eating episodes?

I’m not sure I’d call it guilt exactly… maybe sometimes I feel a little disappointed in myself, like, “Why did I keep doing that?” But I try not to make too big a thing of it. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Would you say that during these episodes, you're eating a large amount of food in a short period of time?

I guess… yes, sometimes. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just stuffing myself every night, but there are nights after supper when I’m putting away the tamales or mole, and I end up having several more servings. And then maybe some pan dulce too, out in the garage.

It’s more than I’d ever put on a plate if everyone was sitting there watching, if that makes sense.
Do these late-night eating episodes cause you a lot of stress or affect your daily life in any way?

It doesn’t stop me from doing what I need to do, really. I still get to my errands and appointments, and I help around the house. So I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But… the mornings after, I do feel kind of sluggish, and I guess I’m not very proud of myself. Like I could’ve handled it better. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel guilty or self-critical after these episodes of eating at night?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d say “often,” exactly. I do get a little down on myself sometimes, like I’m thinking I should’ve stopped sooner. But I try not to sit there beating myself up over it.

Maybe “self-critical” fits a little better than guilty? I’m not sure if that answers what you’re asking.
Do you usually feel guilty after eating at night?

Usually? I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly. Sometimes I think, “Well, that wasn’t my best choice,” and I feel a little bad about it… but I don’t know if I’d call it guilt every time.

I don’t want to overstate it, doctor. It’s more like I’m disappointed in myself here and there, if that makes sense.
Do you feel guilty after these episodes of eating at night?

I guess… not guilty exactly, no. At least not in a big way. I might feel a little disappointed or think I could’ve made a better choice, but I’m not walking around feeling awful about it every time.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever feel guilty after one of these late-night eating episodes?

I don’t think so, not really. Maybe once in a while I feel a little foolish about it, like, “Why did I do that?” But I wouldn’t say guilt is something I really notice afterward.

I hope that’s clear enough.
Have you noticed any significant weight gain since these late-night eating episodes started?

I haven’t really noticed anything significant, no. I mean, my weight can go up and down a little, but I wouldn’t say I’ve seen a big gain from the late-night eating.

At least, not that I’m aware of. Is that helpful?
Do you consistently feel self-critical after these episodes of late-night eating?

I don’t think consistently, no. I mean, I might have a little “well, that wasn’t the best idea” kind of thought, but I wouldn’t say I’m really hard on myself afterward.

At least, not in a way that stands out to me. Is that what you’re asking?
How often do these late-night eating episodes happen?

I guess… looking back, it’s been at least once most weeks. Sometimes it’s more like two nights in a week, especially since my cousin moved in and there are leftovers around more often.

I don’t know if that sounds like a lot, but that’s probably the honest answer.
Do you usually try to hide your late-night eating from others?

I wouldn’t say I’m sneaking around exactly… but, yes, I guess I do try to make sure it’s after the house is quiet. Sometimes I’ll even take it out to the garage.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I wouldn’t really want my cousin or family seeing how much I’m eating, especially when I’m supposed to be the disciplined one. Does that make sense?
Do you always feel at least a little disappointed in yourself after these late-night eating episodes?

Always? I don’t think I’d say always. Maybe sometimes there’s a little regret, like, “I probably didn’t need to do that,” but I’m not sure I notice it every time.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, if that makes sense.
Do you think you could stop eating once you start if you really wanted to?

I’d like to say yes, if I really wanted to, but… I don’t know that that’s always true.

It’s more like once I start picking at the leftovers late at night, part of me is saying, “Okay, that’s enough, Alejandro,” but then my hand just keeps going back anyway. Not every single time maybe, but enough that it worries me. I know that probably sounds like I’m making excuses, but that’s how it feels.
Do you feel like you're a bad person after these episodes of late-night eating?

Bad person? No… I don’t think I’d put it that strongly. I might feel a little foolish or disappointed, like I should’ve had more control, but “bad person” sounds… heavier than what I usually think.

I mean, I don’t like it, but I’m not sitting there thinking I’m terrible. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Do these episodes of late-night eating cause you significant distress?

Significant distress… I’m not sure. I mean, it bothers me some, sure, but I don’t know if I’d call it significant.

I usually try not to dwell on it too much. Maybe I feel uneasy or annoyed with myself for a bit, but then I sort of move on. I don’t want to exaggerate it. Does that answer what you mean?
How many nights in a typical month would you say you have one of these late-night eating episodes?

Maybe… I don’t know, four to eight nights a month? Looking back, it’s probably at least once most weeks, and sometimes more like two nights.

It’s been more noticeable since my cousin moved in, with leftovers around more often. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s probably the honest number.
Do you feel disappointed in yourself after every late-night eating episode?

Every time? No, I don’t think so. Sometimes I’m a bit disappointed, sure, like “well, that wasn’t the best choice,” but other times I just sort of… move on and don’t make too much of it.

I hope that makes sense. I wouldn’t want to overstate it.
